easy.def: A word for me and other people.
examples: Come play with us.
Dad drove us home.
The teacher helped us.

more.def: A word used for the speaker and one or more other people when they are not the ones doing the action.
examples: Our neighbors invited us to their pool party.
The guide showed us how to find animal tracks.
A big wave pushed us back toward the shore.
The pen is usable.
A usable tool.
The room is usable.
The old pen was still usable.
A usable tool hung on the wall.
The room is usable after we clean it.
The usage is correct.
Check the usage.
The word has two usages.

more.def: The way in which something is used, especially a word.
examples: The usage of the word is correct.
Check the usage in the dictionary.
The gadget's usage was easy to learn.

easy.def: To do something with a thing.
examples: I use a pencil.
She uses a spoon.
We used glue.

more.def: To take something and do a job with it.
examples: Please use a ruler to draw a straight line.
Bats use sound to find food in the dark.
He used the old boxes to build a clubhouse.
A key has one use.
This tool has many uses.
The box has no use.

more.def: The purpose that something serves, or the act of putting it to work.
examples: A hammer has one main use, which is hitting nails.
The use of bikes can help keep the air clean.
Old jars can find a new use as flower vases.

easy.def: Able to help you do something.
examples: A map is useful on a trip.
A bag is useful for carrying books.
Glue is useful for fixing things.

more.def: Helpful; able to be used for a purpose.
examples: A flashlight is a useful thing to bring on a camping trip.
The website has useful tips for new gardeners.
Knowing how to swim is a useful skill.
The usefulness of a map.
I see its usefulness.
Its usefulness is clear.
We discussed the usefulness of maps.
The usefulness of the tool was clear.
The book's usefulness was praised.
A broken pen is useless.
The old map was useless.
The umbrella is useless in a storm.

more.def: Not able to do anything helpful.
examples: A pen with no ink is useless.
The old map was useless because the roads had changed.
An umbrella is useless in a strong wind.
Each user has a password.
The user pressed a button.
Users can sign in here.

more.def: A person who uses a thing, especially a computer, a phone or a website.
examples: Each user of the library computer must sign in with a card number.
The new app has millions of users around the world.
A user can change the picture on the screen with a touch.

easy.def: A person who shows people to their seats.
examples: The usher showed us our seats.
An usher stood at the door.
The usher gave us a program.

more.def: A person who shows people to their seats at a wedding, a theater or another event.
examples: The usher led us down the aisle to our seats at the theater.
An usher handed out programs at the school play.
The usher smiled and pointed us toward the front row.

easy.def: To lead someone to a place.
examples: She ushered us inside.
The teacher ushered us to the bus.
Dad ushered the guests in.

more.def: To lead or guide someone to a place, or to be the start of something new.
examples: The teacher ushered the class into the library and showed us to our seats.
The bell ushered us out of the classroom at the end of the day.
A warm breeze ushered in the spring.

easy.def: What happens most of the time.
examples: It is the usual time.
I took the usual road.
He had his usual lunch.

more.def: Happening or done most of the time.
examples: We left at the usual time.
She took her usual seat on the bus.
It was a usual day at school.
I usually walk to school.
We usually eat at six.
She is usually on time.

more.def: In the way that happens most often.
examples: My family usually eats dinner together.
The bus is usually on time.
Dad usually reads the paper in the morning.
